Residency by Investment

Program
Overview

Strategically located at the crossroads of Europe, Asia and the Middle East, Greece is an established European destination with a strong tourism sector, growing economy and attractive real estate market. As a member of the European Union and the Schengen Area, the country offers investors and their families access to a well-connected European base and enhanced international mobility. The Greece Golden Visa Programme, introduced in 2013, enables eligible investors and their families to obtain renewable Greek residency through qualifying investments. The programme offers a flexible route to European residency while providing access to Greece’s Mediterranean lifestyle, strategic location, and long-term opportunities within the European market.

Eligibility Criteria

  1. Main Applicant

    • At least 18 years of age
    • No criminal record
    • Source of funds fulfills investment requirements

  2. Eligibility of Dependents

    • Spouses of the main applicant
    • Children under 21 years of age
    • Dependent parents may also qualify

Program Benefits

  • Obtain residency in an EU member state with visa-free travel throughout the Schengen Area, subject to applicable rules.
  • Choose from multiple qualifying investment routes, including eligible real estate opportunities in selected locations across Greece.
  • Establish a strategic European presence with access to EU markets and broader business and investment opportunities.
  • Enjoy Greece’s Mediterranean lifestyle, rich cultural heritage, quality education and healthcare, combined with a comparatively affordable cost of living.
  • Maintain your Golden Visa without a minimum physical residence requirement, subject to applicable regulations.

About the Greece Program

Your Gateway to European Residency: The Greece Golden Visa

Europe is closer than you think. The Greece Golden Visa Program opens the door to five-year renewable residency in a European country. Schengen Area access, no minimum stay requirement, and a single qualifying investment are what make this option attractive for qualifying investors.

If you’re a non-EU national from Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, or the Philippines, Greek residency by investment program is for you.

Why Choose the Greece Golden Visa?

The Greece Golden Visa is a long-term strategy for global mobility, family security, and lifestyle flexibility.

No minimum physical presence

Unlike standard residence visas that require you to spend a set number of days in-country, the Greece Golden Visa has no general minimum physical-presence requirement. You can continue running your business, travelling freely, and living life on your own terms, while holding a valid European residence permit.

Schengen Area access

This is the benefit that attracts investors from Southeast Asia. Nationals from Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, and the Philippines often face extensive visa requirements for European travel. The Golden Visa removes pre-travel visa restrictions and opens up all Schengen Area member countries.

Family coverage under a single investment

One qualifying investment can extend residency rights to your spouse or civil partner, your unmarried children under 21, and the parents of both you and your spouse or partner. Your family travels the same path, together.

Tax flexibility

The Golden Visa investments do not make you a Greek tax resident. Tax residence is assessed separately under Greek law. The eligible individuals who choose to transfer their tax residence to Greece can access the Article 5A taxation regime. This is a an annual lump-sum of €100,000 on qualifying foreign-source income, for up to 15 tax years. Each qualifying relative covered under the regime adds €20,000.

Investment Routes to Qualify

Route 1: High-Demand Real Estate (€800,000)

This  option applies in the Region of Attica, the Regional Unit of Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini, and Greek islands with populations above 3,100. You must make investment in a single property. For built properties or with an existing building permit, the main spaces must cover at least 120 square meters.

Route 2: Other Areas of Greece (€400,000)

Outside of the high-demand zones, the limit drops to €400,000. The single-property rule and the 120-square-meter minimum still apply. But the previous option of combining multiple smaller apartments to reach the threshold is no longer applicable.

Route 3: Heritage and Change-of-Use Properties (€250,000)

This is available for any property under “Change-of-Use” across Greece. This includes listed or protected buildings needing restoration or reconstruction, and properties whose main spaces are converted from commercial to residential use.

The 120-square-meter minimum isn’t applicable to these properties. But the change of use must be completed before the Golden Visa application is submitted.

Route 4: Greek Startup Investment (€250,000)

For investors who want equity in Greece’s startup ecosystem, a €250,000 investment in a startup registered on the national registry qualifies. Your participation can’t exceed 33% of the company’s capital or voting rights. The business must create at least two new jobs within the first year, and maintain those jobs for at least five years.

Route 5: Financial Investments

This pathway offers three sub-options for investors who prefer capital markets over real estate:

  • €350,000 in qualifying mutual funds or Alternative Investment Funds
  • €500,000 in qualifying Greek companies, real-estate investment companies, Greek government bonds, or qualifying time deposits
  • €800,000 in qualifying listed shares, corporate bonds, and/or Greek government bonds

Each sub-option has specific rules around financial institutions, custody arrangements, investment structure, and minimum holding periods.

Route 6: Hotel or Tourist Accommodation Leases (€400,000–€800,000)

 This option includes long-term tourist accommodation or timeshare contracts of at least 10 years. The minimum contract value is the same as the real estate option: €800,000 in higher-demand regions and eligible islands, and €400,000 in other areas.

What Are the Costs?

Real Estate Taxes and Closing Costs

  • Property Transfer Tax: 3.09% of the taxable value
  • Notary Fees: depends on transaction nature
  • Land Registry and Cadastral Fees: vary by registration and transaction
  • Legal representation, technical due diligence, and other professional fees apply additionally

Government Application Fees

  • Main investor: €2,000
  • Adult family members: €150 per person
  • Minors: exempt from the residence-permit fee
  • Electronic residence-card printing: €16 per card

Additional Costs

  • Private health insurance (required; premiums vary by age, insurer, and coverage)
  • Document preparation: translation, legalization, Apostille, and notarization costs depend on your country of origin
  • Administrative costs are subject to change. Always request a transaction-specific cost estimate.

How to Apply for a Greece Golden Visa?

Step 1: Choose your investment route

Start by identifying which pathway is suitable for your financial goals. If you’re going the real estate route, begin legal and technical due diligence before committing any funds. A property valued at €250,000 does not automatically qualify as a €250,000 Golden Visa property.

Step 2: Engage a Greece Golden Visa lawyer

While optional, this step is highly advisable. An experienced local lawyer can manage title checks, due diligence, payment documentation, powers of attorney, contracts, and immigration compliance. They also coordinate with the notary and all parties involved in the transaction.

Step 3: Open a Greek bank account for your AFM

A Greek Tax Identification Number (AFM) is required for all property and tax transactions. Your legal and financial representatives can help establish the required bank procedures and ensure investment funds move through legally.

Step 4: Finalize the investment

For real estate, the transaction proceeds through the appropriate contractual and notarial process. Payment must go through authorised banking channels. You get a registration cirtificate from Land Registry or Cadastral Office.

Step 5: Submit the Golden Visa application

Applications are submitted electronically through the Greek Ministry of Migration and Asylum’s online platform. Your file should include investment documentation, identity documents, insurance, and all other supporting materials.

Step 6: Complete biometrics and receive your permit

Biometric and identity procedures complete the process. Processing times vary by route, file completeness, and the workload of the competent authority. The current framework ties the five-year validity period to the issuance of the residence card.

Is the Greece Golden Visa Right for You?

For qualifying investors and families seeking European residency with real flexibility, the Greece Golden Visa is one of the most compelling options available today. Entry points start at €250,000 for specific investment categories. The program covers your immediate family under a single application. And it comes with no general minimum physical presence requirement.

So your residency doesn’t have to compete with your existing life.

A Few Limitations Worth Knowing

The Golden Visa does not grant the right to work in Greece. Those intending to work there should consult the separate residence and work permit rules applicable to their situation.

Golden Visa properties can’t generally be used for short-term rentals under the sharing economy model. Short-term rental is defined as a rental of fewer than 60 days without additional services beyond accommodation and bedding. Violations can result in the revocation of your residence permit and an administrative fine of €50,000. Long-term residential leasing, however, remains permitted under Greek rental and tax rules.

The 120-square-meter requirement applies to built properties under the €400,000 and €800,000 real estate routes. Investors can’t merge multiple smaller properties to reach the qualifying threshold.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Do I have to live in Greece to keep my Golden Visa?

No. The Greece Golden Visa has no general minimum physical-presence requirement. You can continue living and working anywhere in the world while maintaining your Greek residence permit. Citizenship by investment is a separate process with its own conditions.

Can I rent out my Golden Visa property?

Long-term residential rental is generally permitted under Greek rental and tax rules. However, short-term rental of fewer than 60 days, without services beyond accommodation and bedding, is not allowed. Violating this restriction can result in revocation of the residence permit and an administrative fine of €50,000.

Will the Greece Golden Visa lead to citizenship?

No. The Golden Visa provides residency, not citizenship. To become a Greek citizen, you must separately apply under Greece’s naturalization framework.

Can I include my parents and my spouse’s parents in the application?

Yes. The Greek framework allows the investor’s spouse or civil partner, unmarried children under 21, and the parents of both spouses or partners to receive residence permits under the same application.

Can I use a mortgage to fund the Golden Visa property purchase?

Any financing arrangement must comply with the program’s statutory investment and payment requirements. Mortgage structures can affect title and qualifying-investment eligibility. A lawyer should review any proposed financing arrangement before you sign anything.

Do I pay taxes in Greece if I obtain the Golden Visa?

The Golden Visa does not automatically trigger Greek tax residence. Tax residence is assessed separately under Greek law. If you choose to transfer your tax residence to Greece, you may be eligible for the Article 5A alternative taxation regime — a €100,000 annual flat tax on qualifying foreign-source income, available for up to 15 tax years.

How long does the Golden Visa last, and can it be renewed?

The residence permit is valid for five years. It can be renewed for equal periods, provided you continue to meet the qualifying investment conditions and other program requirements.
